Rashi on Niddah 21b:11:1.english: And it is more far-reaching - [It is] more stringent.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:12:1.hebrew: אם תוכה מאדים - הבשר מאדים, ואפי' אין שם דם ממש:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:12:1.english: If its interior looks red - the flesh looks red, even if there is no actual blood there.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:13:1.hebrew: כסומכוס - דאמר: תוכה כעמה. ועדיפא מדסומכוס, דאיהו בעי דם ממש:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:13:1.english: Like Sumakhos - who said: its inside is like its outside. And [this ruling] is more far-reaching than that of Sumakhos, for he [Sumakhos] requires actual blood.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:14:1.hebrew: טמאה לידה - ויש לה ימי טוהר, ותשב לזכר ולנקבה: ימי טומאה דנקבה, וימי טוהר דזכר:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:14:1.english: Impure with the impurity of birth - And she has days of purity, and she sits [the periods] for a male and for a female: the days of impurity of a female, and the days of purity of a male.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:14:2.english: White - For it is a kind of flesh.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:14:3.hebrew: זוגא דמן חדייב - שני תלמידי חכמים מאותו מקום:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:14:3.english: A pair from Ḥadyab - Two Torah scholars from that place.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:15:2.hebrew: כסומכוס - דאמר דם שבתוכו מטמא אותה משום נדה:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:15:2.english: Like Sumakhos - Who said that the blood within it renders her impure due to [the status of] a menstruant.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:15:3.hebrew: וקילא מכולהון - מדסומכוס, דלא בעי אגור, ומדר' אחא, דאמר אפילו אין תוכה אלא מאדים:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:15:3.english: And it is more lenient than all of them - [More lenient] than Sumakhos, who does not require accumulated blood, and than Rabbi Aḥa, who said [that the woman is impure] even if its interior is merely reddish.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:1.hebrew: בשפופרת - הכניסה קנה חלול באותו מקום, ונמצא בתוכו דם:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:1.english: In a tube - [If] she inserted a hollow reed into that place, and blood was found inside it.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:2.hebrew: בבשרה - דם יהיה זובה בבשרה, שיצא דרך כותלי בית הרחם ואין מפסיק. והאי קרא בנדה כתיב, ופרשה שניה נאמרה בזבה (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ה): ואשה כי יזוב זוב דמה וגו':
Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:2.english: In her flesh - [The verse means:] "Her issue shall be blood in her flesh" — that it came out through the walls of the uterus, with nothing intervening. And this verse is written regarding a niddah, while the second passage was stated regarding a zavah (Leviticus 15:25): "And if a woman has an issue of her blood, etc."

Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:3.hebrew: שמטמאה בפנים כבחוץ - מאחר שיצא מן המקור לפרוזדור והעמידו כותליה, מיד היא מטמאה. משא"כ בזב ובעל קרי, דאין מטמאין עד שתצא טומאתן לחוץ:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:16:3.english: That she becomes impure inside just as outside - Once [the blood] has left the source [i.e., the uterus] into the vestibule and the walls of the [vaginal canal] have held it, she immediately becomes impure. This is unlike a zav or a ba'al keri, who do not become impure until their impurity emerges outside.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:18:1.hebrew: אם יש בה דם אגור כו' - ומאי שנא משפופרת:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:18:1.english: If it contains accumulated blood, etc. - And what is different [about this] from a tube?

Rashi on Niddah 21b:19:1.hebrew: דרכה של אשה לראות דם בחתיכה - הלכך, כתיב "בבשרה", קרינא ביה, ודמין במינו לא חייץ:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:19:1.english: It is the manner of a woman to see blood in a piece of tissue - Therefore, [it is] written "in her flesh," and we read it as applying [to this case]; [for] blood in its own kind does not constitute a separation.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:1:1.hebrew: הרי זו ספק לידה וספק זיבה - ספק אם זיבה היא וחייבת בקרבן זיבה, ספק אם לידה היא וחייבת בקרבן לידה, ספק אינה לא לידה ולא זיבה ואין עליה קרבן. כיצד? אם ילדה בשלישי ולד גמור, הרי כאן לידה ולא זיבה, ואפי' ראתה דם עם לידתה להשלים ג' ראיות, דקושי סמוך ללידה רחמנא טהרה, לקמן בפ' בנות כותים (נדה דף לו:): "כי יזוב זוב דמה" — דמה מחמת עצמה ולא מחמת ולד. ואם לא היה ולד וראתה דם עם לידתה, הרי כאן זיבה גמורה, דהשתא לאו קושי סמוך ללידה הוא, דאין כאן לידה. ואם לא היה ולד ולא ראתה דם, אין כאן לא לידה ולא זיבה, דשני ימים הוא דחזאי. הלכך מביאה קרבן אחד לאכול בקדשים, דשמא יולדת או זבה היא, ואינו נאכל חטאת העוף שלה, דשמא אינה לא יולדת ולא זבה, דאפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם, ובשלישי לא חזאי וולד נמי לא הואי, והאי קרבן מליקת חולין היא ונבלה:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:1:1.english: It is uncertain whether she is [in the status of] a woman after childbirth or of a zava - It is uncertain whether she is a zava and is obligated in a zava's offering; it is uncertain whether she is a woman who gave birth and is obligated in a childbirth offering; and it is uncertain whether she is neither a woman who gave birth nor a zava, and has no offering [obligation] at all. How so? If she gave birth on the third [day] to a complete offspring, then here there is childbirth and not zava, even if she saw blood with her childbirth, completing three sightings. For the Merciful One declared pure [blood of] hard labor close to childbirth, as [stated] later in the chapter [entitled] Benot Kutim (Niddah 36b): "When her blood flows" — [meaning] blood [that flows] on its own account, and not on account of an offspring. But if there was no offspring and she saw blood with her labor, then here is a full zava, since now it is not hard labor close to childbirth, as there is no childbirth here. And if there was no offspring and she saw no blood, then here is neither childbirth nor zava, because she saw [blood] for only two days. Therefore, she brings one offering to be eaten among the sacrificial foods, since perhaps she is a woman who gave birth or a zava; but her bird sin offering is not eaten, since perhaps she is neither a woman who gave birth nor a zava — for it is possible for the opening of the womb to occur without blood, and on the third [day] she did not see [blood] and there was also no offspring — and this offering is [merely] a non-sacred pinching [of the neck] and a carcass.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:20:1.hebrew: שפיר - עור הולד קודם שנבראו בתוכו גידים ועצמות ובשר:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:20:1.english: Shafir [gestational sac] - The skin of the fetus, before sinews, bones, and flesh were formed within it.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:22:1.hebrew: דפלי פלויי - שיש בה שורות שורות ביקועים מבחוץ, והדם שם:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:22:1.english: That it is split open - That it has rows upon rows of cracks on the outside, and the blood is there.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:1.hebrew: דת"ק - לא מטהר לה אלא מגזרת הכתוב. סבר, האי דם טהור הוא, ומשום חציצה היא טהורה, ומשום גזרת הכתוב. וה"ה לשפופרת, כיון דטעמא משום חציצה הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:1.english: The first tanna - He renders her pure only from the decree of the verse. He holds that this blood is pure, and she is pure because of the interposition, and because of the decree of the verse. And the same applies to a tube, since the reason is because of the interposition.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:2.hebrew: וה"מ דשיעא - חתיכה, והדם בתוכה לא נגע:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:2.english: And this applies only where it is smooth - [Where] the piece [of tissue is smooth], and the blood within it did not touch [the woman's flesh].

Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:3.hebrew: אבל היכא דפלי פלויי - והדם שם, ונוגע ברחם:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:3.english: But where it is cracked - And the blood is there, and touches the womb.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:4.hebrew: טמאה - דקרינן בבשרה, והיינו דקאמרי: אם יש עמה דם, דפלי פלויי טמאה, ואם לאו, טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:23:4.english: Impure - Because we read “in her flesh.” This is what they mean when they say: If there is blood with it, then [if the piece] is cracked, she is impure; and if not, she is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:24:1.hebrew: ורבנן בתראי לא דייקי לישנא דקרא, והאי דמטהרי משום דלאו דם נדה הוא. הלכך לא שנא בתוכה כי שיעא, ולא שנא פלי פלויי דנגע ברחם — טהורה. אבל שפופרת, דם נדה היא — טמאה, דלא דרשינן "בבשרה" אלא לטמאה בפנים כבחוץ:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:24:1.english: And the later Rabbis do not infer from the wording of the verse; and the reason they rule [the woman] pure is that it is not menstrual blood. Therefore, there is no difference whether [the piece of tissue] is inside her smooth [and intact], or whether it is cracked, [so that the blood] touched the womb — she is pure. But [in the case of] a tube, it is menstrual blood, [and] she is impure, for we expound "in her flesh" only to render [her] impure [for blood] inside just as [for blood] outside.

Rashi on Niddah 21b:25:1.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי (דטהורה. דאין דרך הרואה בכך):
Rashi on Niddah 21b:25:1.english: Everyone agrees [on this] (that she is pure, for this is not the way of a woman who sees [blood]).

Rashi on Niddah 21b:2:1.hebrew: שאי אפשר - הלכך, מה נפשך: אם ולד הוא, הרי כאן לידה; ואם אינו ולד, הרי כאן זיבה, דבשלישי חזאי:
Rashi on Niddah 21b:2:1.english: For it is not possible - Therefore, whichever way you look at it: if it is a child, behold, here is a birth; and if it is not a child, behold, here is a [case of] zivah, since she saw [blood] on the third [day].

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:12:1.hebrew: בתוכה מאדים - ואע"ג דלא האדים מבחוץ. ונראה דאם האדים מבחוץ עדיף טפי, אפילו לא האדים מבפנים; כמו דם אגור, דבפנים אינו מועיל אלא לסומכוס, ומבחוץ אפילו לרבנן:
Tosafot on Niddah 21b:12:1.english: "Its interior looks red" - [This applies] even though it did not turn red on the outside. And it appears that if it turned red on the outside, it is even stronger, even if it did not turn red on the inside; like [the case of] congealed blood, where [blood] on the inside is of no avail except according to Sumchus, but on the outside [it is impure] even according to the Rabbis:

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:14:1.english: Zuza - The Arukh explains [that this is] the name of a sage.

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:14:2.hebrew: אם יש בה עצם טמאה לידה - והא דתנן הך קודם הא דדם אגור, דמיירי נמי בנדה ולא בלידה, משום דתני כל דברייתא ברישא:
Tosafot on Niddah 21b:14:2.english: If it contains a bone, [its mother] is impure with the impurity of birth - And [as for the fact] that [the Mishnah] teaches this [ruling] before that [ruling] of "gathered blood," which also deals with a menstruant and not with [the impurity of] birth, [this is] because it teaches the entire [subject of the] baraita first:

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:18:1.hebrew: והאמר רבי שמעון בן יוחי - וא"ת: וליסייעיה ממתני' דבעי עמה דם? וי"ל: היינו משום דקסבר דאינו דם נדות:
Tosafot on Niddah 21b:18:1.english: But Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai said - And if you ask: Let him [the Gemara] bring support from the Mishnah, which requires that blood [come out] with it? And one can say: This is because [the Gemara] holds that it is not menstrual blood:

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:1:1.english: And it is not eaten - For perhaps she did not see [blood] and did not give birth, and she is not required to bring two offerings, because perhaps she saw [blood] and gave birth — for if so, [the blood] is hardship [koshi] adjacent to the birth, and she is pure, since she did not cease [bleeding] for a full day [me'et le'et], as there is such a thing as hardship [koshi] for non-viable births. And so it must be [explained] according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who holds that there is hardship for non-viable births. For if there were no hardship, she would have to bring two offerings: the offering of ziva, which is certainly eaten, and the offering of birth, which, being uncertain, is not eaten. For one offering does not suffice for both ziva and birth, like [the case of] forbidden fat and blood, as we say in the second chapter of Keritot (9b) and later in the chapter [entitled] Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 40a).

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:24:1.hebrew: הא דם נדה טמאה אפילו בשפופרת - וא"ת: מנליה? הא אימא: הא דדם נדה טמאה משום דפלי פלויי, וקרינן ביה "בבשרה", כדמשני אביי לפירש"י. וי"ל: דנראה לו למקשה דרבנן פליגי אמאי דקאמר ר' אליעזר בהדיא "בבשרה" ולא בשפיר ולא בחתיכה, ואתו רבנן למימר דלא מטעם "בבשרה" טהור, אלא משום דאינו דם נדות. הא אם היה דם נדות — טמאה אפילו בשפופרת. דאי דם נדות טהור בשפופרת, אם כן לא הוו פליגי רבנן אמאי דקאמר רבי אליעזר בהדיא:
Tosafot on Niddah 21b:24:1.english: "This [implies that if it is] menstrual blood, she is impure even through a tube" - And if you ask: How does he know this? Say instead: [The inference is that] this — menstrual blood — [renders her] impure because [the tissue] is cracked, and we read about it "in her flesh," as Abaye answers according to Rashi's explanation. And one can answer: It appeared to the questioner that the Rabbis dispute what Rabbi Eliezer said explicitly — "in her flesh," and not [in the case of] a fetal sac or a piece [of tissue] — and the Rabbis come to say that she is pure not because of the reason of "in her flesh," but because it is not menstrual blood. [Hence,] if it were menstrual blood, she would be impure even through a tube. For if menstrual blood through a tube were pure, then the Rabbis would not be disputing what Rabbi Eliezer said explicitly:

Tosafot on Niddah 21b:8:1.hebrew: באפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם קמיפלגי - להך לישנא תימה: דג' מקומות דקאמר ר' יוחנן לעיל (נדה דף יח.) דהלכו חכמים אחר הרוב — למעוטי מאי:
Tosafot on Niddah 21b:8:1.english: "They disagree about whether opening of the womb is possible without blood" - According to this version, it is puzzling: [regarding] the three places in which Rabbi Yochanan said above (Niddah 18a) that the Sages followed the majority — what does [this] exclude?
